   City Council Staff Report

  DATE: December 21, 2022
  AGENDA ITEM NO: 1A

TO:  The Honorable Mayor and City Council
FROM:  Martha Garcia, Director of Finance
SUBJECT:  Adopt a Resolution recognizing the transition of tax collection
  responsibilities from the State Board of Equalization to the California
  Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) and authorize the
  City Manager to contract the CDTFA in accordance with MPMC
  Chapter 3.30

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Adopting a Resolution pursuant to Monterey Park Municipal Code § 3.30.160 that
  recognizes the transition of tax collection responsibilities from the State Board of
  Equalization to the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration
  (CDTFA) and authorizes the City Manager to contract the CDTFA in accordance
  with MPMC Chapter 3.30; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
On December 7, 2022, the City Council certified the results of the November 8, 2022,
municipal election. Among other things, Measure MP was approved by voters and
added Chapter 3.30 to the MPMC to impose a transactions and use tax. MPMC Chapter
3.30 references the “State Board of Equalization” as the California agency responsible
for collecting and remitting the new tax on the City’s behalf.

The successor in interest to the State Board of Equalization is the California Department
of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA). The CDTFA requested that the City Council
identify this new agency as the one responsible for collecting the City’s taxes under
MPMC Chapter 3.30.

Staff recommends adopting the attached draft resolution to allow the City to begin
collecting transactions and use tax effective April 1, 2023.

FISCAL IMPACT:
There is no direct fiscal impact from adopting this resolution, however, adopting the
draft resolution will satisfy the request of the CDTFA and allows the City to begin
collecting transactions and use tax effective April 1, 2023.

  ATTACHMENT 1
  Draft Resolution
   RESOLUTION NO.

  A RESOLUTION ADOPTING REGULATIONS IMPLEMENTING
  MONTEREY PARK MUNICIPAL CODE (MPMC) CHAPTER 3.30
  REGARDING THE MONTEREY PARK TRANSACTIONS AND USE TAX
  (MEASURE MP).

  THE CITY COUNCIL DOES RESOLVE AS FOLLOWS:

SECTION 1: The City Council finds as follows:

  A.  On December 7, 2022, the City Council certified the results of the
  November 8, 2022 municipal election;

  B.  Among other things, Measure MP was approved by voters and added
  Chapter 3.30 to the MPMC to impose a transactions and use tax;

  C.  MPMC Chapter 3.30 references the “State Board of Equalization” as
  the California agency responsible for collecting a remitting the new tax
  on the City’s behalf; and

  D.  The successor in interest to the State Board of Equalization is the
  California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA). The
  CDTFA requested that the City Council identify this new agency as the
  one responsible for collecting the City’s taxes under MPMC Chapter
  3.30.

SECTION 2: Authority. Pursuant to MPMC § 3.30.160, the City Council finds that all
references within MPMC Chapter 3.30 to the “State Board of Equalization” are
references to the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA). The
City Manager is authorized to implement this Section as appropriate including, without
limitation, providing a certified copy of this Resolution to the CDTFA for purposes of
ensuring the smooth transition of services.

SECTION 3: Interpretation. This Resolution should be interpreted as broadly as
possible in order to implement the voter’s intention of adopting Measure MP.

SECTION 4: Severability. If any part of this Ordinance or its application is deemed
invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, the city council intends that such invalidity
will not affect the effectiveness of the remaining provisions or applications and, to this
end, the provisions of this Ordinance are severable.

SECTION 5: Electronic Signatures. This Ordinance may be executed with electronic
signatures in accordance with Government Code §16.5. Such electronic signatures will
be treated in all respects as having the same effect as an original signature.

SECTION 6: Effective Date. This Resolution is effective immediately upon adoption.
